items.statement: Credit bureau universe: 40 crore total, ~25 crore income-generating; Finbud over-indexed on salaried borrowers
items.quote: There are 40 crore people on the bureau. If I was to remove people who are on the agri-side or micro finance loans, etc., and see where FinBud, may not be a future participant, that number shrinks to around 25 crores.

items.statement: Secured INR 9,840 crore incremental lifetime bookings including INR 1,760 crore exports, additive to FY25 VAR of INR 4,380 crore
items.quote: Now, I am also very happy to report that we have secured important strategic wins of INR98.4 billion, which is INR9,840 crores, in incremental lifetime bookings, including INR17.6 billion of exports, which is about INR1,760 crores.

items.statement: Bookings represent lifetime VAR potential from awarded programs not yet in production, enhancing revenue visibility over next 5-6 years
items.quote: These bookings represent lifetime value-added revenue potential from awarded programs, which are yet to start production and materially enhance the company's revenue visibility over the next five to six years approximately.

items.statement: VAR grew 8.9% YoY in Q2FY26 and 8.2% YoY in H1FY26, outperforming served market growth of 5% in Q2 and 4% in H1
items.quote: For Q2FY26, value-added revenue stood at INR11,515 million, a growth of 8.9% year-on-year, and it has been supported by stronger customer demand across key programs both in domestic as well as export markets.

items.statement: EBITDA margins may be soft in near term due to listed company costs (management, compliance, legal, IT) but expected to absorb as revenue grows
items.quote: We expect EBITDA to be a bit soft, but with increase in the revenue in the coming years, these additional costs will get absorbed as we progress and we come back to the same levels.

items.statement: H1FY26 capex INR 246 million, in line with planned investment; future capex for capacity expansion, technology upgrade, and transfer from other Tenneco regions to be funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Capex for period stood at I NR246 million, and that is in line with the planned investment across our facilities and our localization roadmap

items.statement: Planning capacity expansion including new plants over coming years aligned with order book visibility and growth plans, covering both Clean Air and Advanced Ride Technologies
items.quote: So, we would be investing in line with the growth plans that we have, incl uding putting up the new plants in the coming years

items.statement: Exports grew from 5% to 7-8% of total; export bookings include both third-party OEMs and Tenneco Global; exports carry higher margins and expected to grow faster than domestic
items.quote: If you remember our roadshows and press conferences, we always said, look, we started from a low base of only 5% product exports. And now, if you look at our Q2 FY26 numbers, we're already somewhere around 7% or 8%.

items.statement: TREM 5 norms for commercial vehicles expected around 2027 (FY27), will drive significant content growth in Clean Air; TREM 5 bookings already in order book
items.quote: It might be FY27, it might be early or later FY27. We think it'll be around 2027. And that's when those norms will very positively impact our sales revenue.

items.statement: H1FY26 cash conversion cycle negative 22 days; operating cash flow INR 11,220 million; continue to operate with negative working capital intensity
items.quote: Our cash conversion cycle for H1 FY26 stood at negative 22 days, underscoring the capital-efficient nature of our business model.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; all capex and working capital needs met through internal accruals
items.quote: We continue to stay debt-free and have been meeting all our requirements in terms of capex as well as working capital to internal accruals.

items.statement: Precious metal substrate cost is pass-through; 2.5% royalty on revenue from operations benchmarked and approved; royalty impact on margins negligible
items.quote: Now, in terms of royalty, we are paying 2.5% royalty to our corporate, which is kind of, this being a related party transaction, it has been, there has been a benchmarking that has been done.

items.statement: Strategic Clean Air entry into leading Japanese passenger vehicle OEM (previously untapped white space); major Advanced Ride Technologies win with prominent Indian OEM securing #1 position in shock absorbers
items.quote: These bookings include a strategic clean air business entry into a leading Japanese passenger vehicle OEM, which was previously untapped white space for us.

items.statement: Shock absorber market share increased from 48% to 52% (per CRISIL); limited competitors for advanced suspension technologies with electronic controls and systems integration
items.quote: You would have seen from the DRHP to the RHP that 48% has already gone to 52% market share, which is again from CRISIL.

items.statement: Clean Air & Powertrain Q2FY26 revenue INR 5,702 million (+3% YoY); Advanced Ride Technologies Q2FY26 revenue INR 5,813 million (+15.4% YoY)
items.quote: Looking at our segments, Clean Air and Powertrain solutions delivered revenue of INR5,702 million in Q2 FY26, growing 3% year-on-year, while advanced ride technologies delivered INR5,813 million, up by 15.4%.

items.statement: Headwinds: commercial truck market at 5-year low, potential PV B/C/D segment slowdown, new labor code implications unclear; macro risks affect all players
items.quote: Our headwinds are more about the general market. What happens to commercial trucks. For example, the road infrastructure, we're going through a 5-year low and commercial trucks don't seem to be growing in a big way.

items.statement: Adding leadership and key resources (HR, IT, finance, compliance) for public company requirements; staggering hires over time to manage cost impact
items.quote: This cost, what we're talking about, which has a sort of a soft impact on EBI TDA is because of the fire of new leaders. New leadership, there's also strengthening of HR, IT, finance, because once you go to a public entity, you have to hire certain key resources to manage things like compliances and HR-related labor laws, etcetera

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 54.14 crore as of the call date, split across defence/government (Rs 23.81 cr), power sector (Rs 28.87 cr) and others (Rs 1.46 cr).
items.quote: Hamare pass defense and government ke, 23.81 crore ke order hath me hain, power sector k 28.87 ke hain, others 1.46 ke hain, and 54.14 crore ks order in hand hain.

items.statement: Management declined to give specific forward revenue guidance, pointing investors to compare H1 FY26 results with prior periods for trend extrapolation.
items.quote: Voh toh maine aapko btaya na aap hmara half yearly result dekh lijiye, pichle saal ka half yearly result dekh lijiye, pichle saal ka full year result dekh lijiye or comparision kr lijiye or apna anuman lga lijiye.

items.statement: EBITDA margins around 26-26.5% are described as stable.
items.quote: Are your margins stable hai jo apne 26-26.5% karte hai? Sukesh Naithani: stable hai.

items.statement: Power distribution utilities are increasingly seeking predictive analysis services due to financial stress and the need for performance improvement.
items.quote: With the onset of this growing consciousness that they have to bring about a better financial improvement in their performance, they are increasingly asking us for our services.

items.statement: Engineering team size increased to over 165 people to handle multi-domain, multi-client delivery.
items.quote: So, since we have to work on multiple domain s, we have to work on multiple clients at the same time, so on this day, we have enhanced our engineering team size to 165, or rather a little more than that.

items.statement: Actively pursuing acquisition of a semiconductor design services company (8-9 years vintage, experienced management) and in due diligence; also signed strategic alliance with Kaynes Semicon for end-to-end product design.
items.quote: We have shortlisted or narrowed down one company, and we are in a very active discussion with that company in terms of the acquisition, and we are in the process of due diligence right now.

items.statement: India engineering simulation market estimated at $7.9 billion by 2030 with ~21% CAGR per Grand View Research.
items.quote: They had estimated that the India's emission market would reach around 7.9 billion by 2030, with that as a CGR of around 21%.

items.statement: India cybersecurity market expected to grow at >17% CAGR to $22+ billion by 2032.
items.quote: it's, expected to show, more than 17% CAGR in the coming years, and it is expected to hit about 22+ billion dollars in India by year 2032

items.statement: Global semiconductor market projected at 12-14% CAGR; India semiconductor market seen at ~$110 billion by 2030.
items.quote: Globally, if you look at the growth rate that is expected is about 12 -14% CAGR. And India is not an exception there, so we are looking at about, 110 billion, kind of a market by, 2030.

items.statement: Actively pursuing proposals in seven countries (Saudi, Oman, Nigeria, Turkey, Cameroon, etc.) via Dubai office; acquisition target has US customers and offshore centres.
items.quote: We are working… right now, the proposal is going with the seven countries. not only Dubai, But Saudi, Oman, then Nigeria, Turkey, Cameroon, various countries.

items.statement: Revenue not segmented by vertical yet due to overlapping technologies; Semicon subsidiary to be reported separately when it scales.
items.quote: That kind of breakup, will… as such, is still not the statutory requirement, right? But, if… just like the Semicon, Semicon is a different company. So even if tomorrow we decide that one part… one particular division is growing big, their entire economics and, psychology is going to be different, then we can have the different, kind of, vertical for that. But so

items.statement: AMC on software licences varies 10-20% per year; sometimes first-year AMC free, sometimes starts after 90 days or one year, negotiated per order.
items.quote: It is varied. Some, some AMC is even 10%. Rajesh Jain: Okay, so between 10 to 20%, basically. Sukesh Naithani: 10-20%, or who pehle saal bhi aa sakti hai ya first year ka AMC aapko free dena padta hain product ke sath, next year se shuru

items.statement: 300 clients in portfolio with repeat orders; client acquisition driven by reference from successful deliveries.
items.quote: 300 client hamare portfolio me hain, jo hamare sath, hamare clientele list me hain, or jinke saath repeated orders chalte rehte hain.

items.statement: Large tenders (Rs 40-50 cr+) require 5-6 levels of signature approval; process learned and now factored into execution planning.
items.quote: Jab ham kisi bade tender pe kaam karte hain jiska tenure, jiska tune 40-50 cr se upper hoga , to usme signature authorities alag alag hoti hain. Aapko approval jo hain 2-3 level pe lena padta hain, 5-6 level pe lena padta hain.

items.statement: Raghu Panicker (CEO Kaynes Semicon, 30+ years exp) appointed strategic advisor for semiconductor business.
items.quote: we have experience leadership. We have got Raghu Panicker as the strategic advisor. He's the current CEO of Ka ynes Semicon, but he comes with 30 + years of experience

items.statement: No specific capex plan disclosed; investment focused on talent acquisition for niche semiconductor capabilities.
items.quote: We will have to have scalable, you know, talent base, because the existing talent is satisfying our existing customers, but if we want to acquire some new clients and get into niche areas, definitely we'll have to look into you know, expertise from the industry who can come on board with us.

items.statement: Previous guidance missed due to shift to larger orders with longer procedural timelines, not order loss; all opportunities intact.
items.quote: Last time ki, yes, jo hamne kaha tha vo pura nahi hua. Uski vagah ye nahi thi ki ham hamare order koi miss hue ya hamari koi opportunity loss hui. Hamari sari opportunities pipeline mein ai, ya kuch order aage. Pehle usme differences ye aya tha, ki pehle ham 10 ya 12 ya 15cr ke order lete the. Ab ham bade orders pe kaam karte hain.

items.statement: Cybersecurity division (1 year old) secured strategic defence business; daily improvement across all four verticals.
items.quote: log abhi cyber security mai hum abhi pichle 1 saal se aaye hain But 1 saal se humne Strategical Defense ke business ko liya hain Joki bohot badi achievement hai

items.statement: Revenue mix over 3-5 years depends on market potential and execution capability; management refuses to quantify segment split.
items.quote: 3 se 5 saal ka Deepak ji pehle he humne aapko btaya hai humne ek statistical data aapko di ya ki ye h market itna ba r rah hain yeh market itna bar raha hain. Aap hmare present ke business ko dekhiye hum kha pe hain, kitna bd sakta hain voh depend karta hain ki hamari capability mein, financial powers mein, ya sari chize hain joh ki depend karte hai.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 to be better than H1 and sees double-digit revenue growth of 14-15% for FY26 versus FY25.
items.quote: H2 will be better than H1 but you can very well imagine that if H1 is doing almost 23 0-232 so if you add 230 even my one. So now the other I will ask him. You have to really prove it for every growth is coming, but to answer you, yes, we are looking very, very optimistic.

items.statement: Vision to reach INR 1,000 crore revenue in the next three to five years.
items.quote: Our next milestone is 1000 crores and to be achieved in next three to five years.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 is about INR 50 crore, likely to be maintained or slightly lower; FY27 capex still being compiled.
items.quote: I think for FY 26, we have already announced in our capex. Look at all the total spend will be about 50 crores and now it's almost towards the end of the year and we are going to maintain this and maybe a crossover, less of it not higher than this, but definitely.

items.statement: Received second nomination for transmission parts from a large premium 2-wheeler OEM; SOP expected July 2027 at Gajraula plant.
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have got a second nomination now from the same OEM for the transmission part of a gearbox assembly, this p roject again falls under the high-volume business segment for the new engine category which is currently not available in the market. So, and I'm happy to share that this project we will be executing at G ajraula plant and the SOP is expected to start from July 2027

items.statement: TVS RTX 310 and Norton projects launched; production started in November 2025, volumes expected to pick up in 2026.
items.quote: TVS has launched this bike at exhibition in Italy, and you know this is the first time that two top models were launched had a global launch in Italy, where TV has had launched a new vehicle called RTX 310, and then they had launched in Norton brand as a global brand and I'm proud to say that all both the models and products are from your company. Mr. Tej Patel Great. Great. Mr. Gursharan Singh An

items.statement: BMW parking lock mechanism project in pre-series phase; SOP expected 2026.
items.quote: Right now, they're sample serious phases are going on. So that is also adding to the value because the pre -series phases are also off quite good numbers. It runs in 2026.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained above 24% in Q1 and Q2 FY26; Q2 EBITDA margin 24.25%, H1 24.52%.
items.quote: we have been able to consistently maintain our EBITDA margin above 24% from now, from Q1 and Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Total debt reduced from INR 305 crore to INR 218 crore (28% decrease) since March 2025; debt-to-equity at 0.67x; target to keep debt-to-equity below 1x.
items.quote: our overall total debt has c ome down from 305 crores to 218 crores from last from 31st March till now. So, which is a decrease of almost 28% and accordingly most of our financial ratios have changed significantly, on debt by equity is close 0.67.

items.statement: Credit rating reaffirmed at CARE A- (long term) and A2+ (short term); outlook revised from stable to positive; rated facilities reduced by INR 63.55 crore to INR 273.38 crore.
items.quote: I'm happy to share that again this year our external credit rating has been reaffirmed by care as a minus for long term banking facilities and A2 plus for short term banking facilities. But I'm happy to share that they have revised the outlook from being stable to positive. So th at's an upgrade on the outlook side.

items.statement: Cash generation from operations grew ~50% to INR 29.87 crore in H1 FY26 vs INR 19.81 crore in H1 FY25.
items.quote: Our cash from generation has grown from 19.81 crores to 29.87 crores in H1 of this year as compared to H1 of last year, representing a growth of close to 50%.

items.statement: Euro appreciation benefited non-operating income by INR 8-10 crore in H1 FY26; company uses natural hedge via pre-shipment credit in foreign currency.
items.quote: So overall, if you look at the picture is then about the overall euro in H1 it's about between 8 to 10 crores of impact.

items.statement: Technical collaboration with AARK Engineering GmbH (Germany) enables shift from build-to-print to concept-to-print (product design, validation, material selection).
items.quote: Now with this technical collaboration with A ARK Engineering , now we will have a capability to do the product designing right from the inception of the product.

items.statement: KTM production restarted 24 July 2025; currently at 40-50% of pre-bankruptcy levels; expected to improve in 2026.
items.quote: KTM has started his production and precisely it started on 22nd of July and that really you can also understand that if complete remains stopped for six 7 -8 months. So definitely it will have many challenges so they are really ramping up. They have ambitious to ramp up, but they are having some supply challenges because they have to you know, that was a global company, they had a glo bal customer

items.statement: Europe reached a plateau in 2024-25; management expects improvement driven by defence and infrastructure spending; euro appreciated 6-7% vs dollar in last six months.
items.quote: Europe achieved a plateau in 2024 and 2025. So, whatever now is going to happen, it is going to happen in the plus direction only because of political scenario. Europeans are spending in a big way into infrastructure projects, particularly in the defence projects and particularly energy sector.

items.statement: Participated in defence manufacturing conclave at Jabalpur (Nov 7-9, 2025) to explore entry into defence sector as a sustainable long-term initiative.
items.quote: this is a kind of initiative which we get entry in a sustainable level in the near future because India is fast becoming a hub for defence manufacturing. So, this is a kind of initial first step where we are trying to take into this, let's really see how it takes.

items.statement: No new projects contributed to H1 FY26 revenue growth; growth driven by recovery in existing programs and base effect.
items.quote: So, there is absolutely no new project which has contributed to being revenue growth. BMW cars prototyping is happening somewhere. The pickup is good there. Second many for existing projects which were earlier, you know in last year our plan was to grow 25 -30%.

items.statement: Aims to sustain or exceed 15% revenue CAGR and grow faster than the market over the medium to long term
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim to sustain if not exceed this momentum and continue to grow faster than the overall market that is a key direction that we are going in and this will be driven by a couple of factors first, we want to realise the full potential of our existing network.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA to grow faster than the historical 18% CAGR driven by operational efficiencies and operating leverage
items.quote: And we expect our EBITDA to grow at a faster pace than this historical CAG R and which will be driven by a couple of measures again

items.statement: Targets at least 20% plus ROCE over the next five years
items.quote: So overall, I feel we expect a trend of at least a 20% plus ROCE over the next five years.

items.statement: Expects corporate EBITDA margin to reach 21%-22% in near term and 27%-28% pre-corporate cost in long term (4-5 years)
items.quote: We are at 19% in Q2. We have delivered an EBITDA margin of 19% in Q2. And as I had said, based on our higher-than-market revenue growth and operating leverage, we expect the margins to grow faster than the historical trend. Obviously, it is upwards of 21%, 22%.

items.statement: Expects 4%-5% annual realisation improvement and 9%-10% volume growth in near to midterm
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at 4% to 5% reali sation improvement every year. And the volume growth will be in the region of 9% to 10

items.statement: Targets revenue potential of 100% (from current 56%) in 4-5 years at existing price points
items.quote: It is practical and doable because we have taken optimal occupancy and utilisation. We have not taken 100% occupancy and 100% utili sation. These are practically doable revenue numbers at existing price points

items.statement: Plans Rs.600-700 crore capex over next 2-3 years, including Rs.300 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: So in the next two to three years, it is about Rs. 600 crore to Rs.700 crore, out of which about Rs.300 crore will be maintenance capex.

items.statement: Maintenance capex expected at Rs.90-100 crore annually; expansion capex Rs.500-600 crore over 2-3 years
items.value: Rs.90 crore to Rs.100 crore annually
items.quote: Now, as the size of the network has grown, we expect maintenance capex to be in the range of Rs.90 crore to Rs.100 crore annually. In addition, we would like to spend additional Rs.500 crore to Rs.600 crore over the next two, three years to fund expansion.

items.statement: Plans 1,000 bed addition: ~700 beds brownfield (Ahmedabad, Vizag, Baroda, Cuttack) and 200-400 beds greenfield (Pune, Surat, Varanasi, Kanpur)
items.quote: I think brownfield will add about 700 beds through that route. And in markets like Ahmedabad, Vizag, Baroda, Cuttack, so that is our brownfield expansion plan. And as far as greenfield expansion is concerned, in newer cities like Pune, Surat, Varanasi, Kanpur, to name a few, while it is just indicative, we have identified 10 to 12 cities in that bucket, that will be about 200 to 400 beds.

items.statement: Incremental revenue split: 70-75% from existing centres, 10-15% brownfield, 8-10% greenfield over 4-5 years
items.quote: Our big part of our incremental revenue, about 70% -75% of our incremental revenue is going to come from existing centres, right? 10%-15% is going to come from brownfield expansion, and about 8%-10% is going to come from the greenfield expansion that we have, planned for.

items.statement: Mature centres (>Rs.10 crore/month) deliver 25% EBITDA pre-corporate cost and 27% pre-corporate ROCE
items.quote: Our mature centres doing more than Rs.10 crore of revenue are already delivering an EBITDA of 25% pre corporate cost. So as more and more centres come into this bucket, our EBITDA margins would grow at a healthy CAGR.

items.statement: Procurement identified as a lever to improve margins
items.quote: That is right. Procurement is going to be also one of the levers that we are going to work on to improve margins.

items.statement: Undertaking annual pricing benchmarking exercise across markets; results expected in couple of weeks
items.quote: From time to time, we undertake an exercise to understand where we are, in terms of pricing vis-à-vis our competitors, and currently also we have undertaken that exercise which should get over in the next couple of weeks.

items.statement: Revenue split: Radiation 20%, Medical Oncology 42%, balance Diagnostics and Surgical
items.quote: As far as your question on the split is concerned, radiation is today 20% of our overall revenue, medical is about 42%, and the balance is driven by diagnostics and surgeries, surgical.

items.statement: Institutional payor mix 34% in FY2025; CGHS is 12%-13% of institutional business
items.quote: In that institutional business, CGHS is in the range of 12% to 13% from the institutional business.

items.statement: Claims superior clinical outcomes vs multi-specialty hospitals; sees volume shift to single-specialty centres as awareness rises
items.quote: Cancer is a very complex disease to handle and it requires a super-speciality focus, which we have delivered and shown that clinical outcomes that we deliver are far superior to multi-speciality hospitals.

items.statement: Added senior leaders: Head of Clinical Strategy, CMO, CIO, Heads of International and Domestic Sales
items.quote: We have added some new roles in the team and we have on-boarded some senior leaders, from a reputed organization in the sector into the team. As I said, and I want to just reiterate that, roles like Head of Clinical Strategy to drive focus on identifying good clinical talent, good oncologists across our network and on-board them.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA at 2.5x; targets maintaining 2-2.5x pre-Ind AS; capex funded via internal accruals and borrowing headroom
items.quote: Net debt to EBITDA ratio is two-and-a-half times today and we are comfortable with that right now. And a lot of this capex funding is going to come from internal accruals, because we are mindful of this leverage ratio.

items.statement: Evaluating equity-debt ratio; will take appropriate call at appropriate time
items.quote: So, we are evaluating our equity and debt ratio. And at an appropriate time, we will take an appropriate call on that.

items.statement: Evaluating strategic options for Milann vertical, including potential divestment
items.quote: I think one of the options, while we are still evaluating, just to be very clear, could be divestment of this vertical. But again, not a definitive answer at this point in time, because we are evaluating various options.

items.statement: Mature centre vintage 10+ years; mid bucket 6-7 years; smaller centres <5 years or limited by size
items.quote: The bucket which has centres doing more than Rs.10 crore per month are about 10 years plus vintage and the middle bucket that I mentioned are about six to seven years.

items.statement: Mature centre growth trajectory: 1x asset turnover, 15-20% EBITDA margin, 15-20% ROCE in 4-5 years
items.quote: 1x asset turnover in four to five years and that is the typical growth trajectory we take. Also a 15% to 20% EBITDA margin in the same time period and 15% to 20% ROCE in the same time period.

items.statement: Refrains from centre-level guidance; adopts cluster-based approach; some centres require turnaround via clinical talent, programs, infrastructure
items.quote: We want to refrain from giving centre-wise guidance today. We are looking at a cluster-based approach to our business. And all the clusters have done well in the past. However, to answer this question specifically, there have been concerns in the past about some of our centres.

items.statement: Doctor incentive model primarily fixed retainer; fee-for-service in some markets (e.g., Western cluster); no plan to change
items.quote: I think many of our doctors are on a retainer fixed model. And I think that is the preferred model that we have in our system, people who are full timers with us. But of course, different markets have different nuances, like the Western cluster, many of the doctors prefer to be on a fee for service model.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue target of Rs 250 crore; FY27 target of Rs 300-310 crore console; peak capacity revenue of Rs 350 crore by FY28
items.quote: last year our consolidate turnover was 200 crores and current year we are well on course to achieve 250 crores. As we mentioned as standard performance of 228 crores and a consolidated performance of 250 crores.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue estimated at Rs 300-310 crore; peak capacity of Rs 350 crore expected by FY28
items.quote: to be very conservative, a console level of 300 to 310 crores will be a fairly reasonable estimation of the next year's overall performance.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 65 crore largely deployed; solid tyre plant production started, mixing plant in final commissioning; one tyre building machine pending by month-end
items.quote: except for one tyre building machine which is expected to come by month end almost all the projects are nearing completion and the substantial amounts have been released.

items.statement: Total debt expected at Rs 110 crore post capex completion; working capital increase marginal; export packing credit at 6.35%, term loans at 9%, working capital at 9-10%
items.quote: overall this is the status and as far as the completion of the project is concerned, there will always be some amounts which are paid only on performance.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 17.75% vs 16.51% YoY; net profit margin 7.56% vs 6.38%; management expects same margin trend in H2 despite US tariff impact
items.quote: EBITDA margins also have jumped from 16.51 to 17.75 in the six months. And I think overall we're glad to inform you that in spite of the difficult market situation in US and other markets, I think Emerald is one company which has registered an increase in the US business.

items.statement: Mixing plant internalisation to yield cost savings from Q4 FY26; full benefit in FY27; no major depreciation drag expected
items.quote: the cost savings that comes out of the mixing unit will accrual only for three months, because almost nine months have gone by, so there won't be any major impact in the profitability that you would expect. We'll continue the same trend.

items.statement: US business grew slightly in H1 despite tariffs; Europe significant increase; Australia, Latin America, Saudi Arabia, South Africa identified as growth markets
items.quote: in the first six months the US market business has slightly grown over the last year and the Europe has shown significant increase in performance. And I think there are two, three other markets which are in the cusp of major improvement in volume which are Australia, Latin America and Saudi Arabia and southern Africa.

items.statement: Solid tyres 50%, pneumatic 50% of revenue; within solid: 10% press-on bands, 12% wheel rims; pneumatic: 40% tyre alone, 10% tyre+wheel; solid tyres carry higher margins due to application engineering
items.quote: Sir, if you take pneumatic and solid is 50-50 and within solid tyre you will have 10% Press on bands, pneumatics balance, solid tyres, tyres alone.

items.statement: Raw material prices steady; able to pass on cost increases via CM Index; new AXIMO super-premium solid tyre priced 10% higher; US customers absorbed tariff hit, minimal discount given
items.quote: Yeah, raw material if you're looking at raw material prices, it has been fairly steady.

items.statement: 83% export revenue; domestic 50/50 OEM-replacement; export 20% OEM / 80% replacement; key domestic OEMs: Toyota, JCB, ACE, Godrej, Doosan; global focus on small/medium OEMs
items.quote: 83% of the revenue has come from export, Sir.

items.statement: Pneumatic capacity expanding from 12 to 30 tonnes/day; solid tyre capacity doubled; mixing plant internalisation completes backward integration; greenfield needed beyond 350 crore peak
items.quote: Pneumatic tyres has a different manufacturing process. Solid tyres have a different manufacturing process, so you can't. In a pneumatic process -- so the mixing remains the same but when it comes to downstream in a building of tyres, curing of tyres, these are 2 different methods by which we do.

items.statement: Exports to US, Europe, Middle East, Australia, Latin America, South Africa, Russia; FOB terms insulate from freight volatility; no government export benefits received yet despite rupee at 90
items.quote: Generally, we don't take CIF shipments. We always and that was one reason during COVID when the freight rates post COVID the freight rates went to Sky High, Emerald was one company which never had an impact on its profitability or supply chain purely because we thought our core focus is to make a product.

items.statement: Inventory and debtor days higher than peers due to application-specific stocking (28 formulations); South Africa receivables include stock-in-trade; recovery of Rs 3.5-4 cr in last 6 months, balance expected by Mar-26
items.quote: These are not outstanding unreceivable. These are tyres physically available in these places for marketing to the customers.

items.statement: Acquired Apnar Pharma Private Limited, which operates a USFDA-approved facility in Gujarat, plus five ANDAs formerly owned by Sandoz.
items.quote: Senores will acquire Apnar Pharma for a total enterprise value of Rs.91 crores.

items.statement: Transaction structure: Rs 76 crore of debt assumed and refinanced; Rs 15 crore equity paid in two tranches funded from IPO proceeds and internal accruals.
items.quote: Out of this Rs. 91 crores, Rs.76 crores represents debt associated with the facility and other expenses, which will be assumed by Senores and refinanced at a lower interest rate as we move forward. The remaining Rs.15 crores will be paid as equity in two tranches.

items.statement: Deal closure timeline: 75% by March 2026, remaining 25% by October 2026.
items.quote: 75% of the transaction is expected to close by March '26 and the remaining 25% by October 2026.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for the acquired facility: Rs 100-120 crore in FY27, peaking at Rs 250 crore by FY28.
items.quote: Our post acquisition, we expect upwards to about Rs. 100 crore of revenue coming out of this plant in next year from FY'27. Peak revenue from the current existing infrastructure that they have would be around Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for the acquired facility: 20-30% in FY27, 30%+ in first full year of operation.
items.quote: Profitability-wise, what we expect is at the best Rs. 100 crore plus revenue next year, would be almost 20%-30% of EBITDA is what we are expecting from this facility.

items.statement: Minimal incremental capex of Rs 5-7 crore for facility upgrades; no major capacity capex needed until decent utilization is reached.
items.quote: I might spend another Rs. 5 crores-Rs. 7 crores quickly to upgrade a few of the facilities.

items.statement: Acquired facility has installed capacity of 275 million capsules annually (scalable to 600 million); current production ~225 million units, potential to 500 million.
items.quote: The plant has an installed capacity of annually about 275 million capsules, scalable to 600 million. Current capsule production stands about 225 million units with the potential to increase to 500 million.

items.statement: US Atlanta facility currently at 1.2-1.3 billion units capacity with 60-70% utilization; targeting 2 billion units capacity and 70% utilization (1.3-1.4 billion output) in 2 years.
items.quote: We are currently about between 1.2 billion to 1.3 billion production capacity in Atlanta today, we are at about 60% to 70% utilization. And we feel that the utilization percentage in the US will max at about 70%.

items.statement: Plan to shift 100-150 million units of non-controlled products from US to India facility over time via CBE-30 and PAS routes.
items.quote: Part of that US and the new products that we have will come to India, which will be incremental about 100 million-150 million, at a high level as we consider today.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from moving lower-margin products to India (lower cost) and freeing US capacity for higher-margin CDMO/controlled substance business.
items.quote: The cost associated with those products, once it moves to India, the cost also significantly reduces, right? So, that's another strategic advantage. So, overall, I become competitive on slightly on a product that are margin compressed.

items.statement: Overall margin profile not expected to change much; possible 100-200 bps increment as production scales and registrations progress.
items.quote: Overall margin profile, we do not think that margin profile will change much, maybe 100-200 basis points increment you probably would see.

items.statement: Consolidated debt-equity to remain below 0.5x after assuming Apnar's Rs 75 crore debt (mostly working capital, Rs 25 crore long-term); long-term debt to stay around Rs 50-55 crore.
items.quote: Overall, if we see consolidated level, still we are at below 0.5% of debt equities, which is quite comfortable for us. Even looking, even taking into consideration of Apnar debt, that consolidated level will be still below 0.5% to afford debt equity.

items.statement: Last USFDA inspection in FY23; change-of-ownership inspection expected after filing.
items.quote: The inspections happened around FY'22 or FY'23, as we speak. So probably the moment the change of ownership that has been put it up in the FDA, I think the inspection can come.

items.quote: Overall, the acquisition enhances scalability, enables accelerated product launches, improves operating leverage and margins and expands CDMO-CMO opportunities positioning Senores for sustained growth and to create long-term shareholder value.

items.statement: UL approval enables US exports; pre-approved supplier to Power Grid Corporation; new products like CTC require PGCIL approvals but many transformer orders to electricity boards need no approvals.
items.quote: Our UL approval enables exports to the US market, and we are pre-approved suppliers to Power Grid Corporation of India Limited.

items.statement: H1 FY2026 EBITDA without other income grew 19% to Rs.34 Crores; EBITDA margin 4.3% (+50 bps); PAT grew ~30% to Rs.23 Crores; PAT margin 2.8%; EPS Rs.1.41 (+29%).
items.quote: During the half year, our revenues increased by about 5.1% year -on-year basis to Rs.793 Crores from Rs.750 Crores in the previous corresponding period. H1 FY2026 EBITDA without other income grew by 19% to Rs. 34 Crores. The EBITDA margin increased to 4.3% an improvement of 50 basis points. PA T grew nearly 30% to Rs. 23 Crores with a PAT margin increase to 2.8% while EPS grew 29% to Rs.1.41.

items.statement: 3-year CAGR (FY2023-25): Revenue 21.23%, EBITDA 33.86%, PAT 37.86%, Net worth 28.91%.
items.quote: Looking at our three -year track record from FY2023 to 2025, our revenue CAGR grew by 21.23% , EBITDA CAGR grew by 33.86% and PAT CAGR at 37.86%. Net worth has compounded at 28.91%.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs.274 Crores fresh issue; Rs.140 Crores for capex at ALCU, Rs.100 Crores for debt repayment.
items.quote: On IPO proceeds, as committed we are prudently deploying the fresh issue funds our IPO raised Rs.274 Crores, Rs. 140 Crores is allocated for capital expenditure at A LCU Industries ; this will nearly double our capacity to 37,680 metric tons and enable new product lines. The expansion is progressing as planned. Rs.100 Crores is for repayment of borrowings

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; key personnel: Shailesh Rathi (MD), Naveen Pachisia (CFO), Arun Maheshwari (Head Finance).
items.quote: From the management side, we have Mr. Shailesh Rathi, Managing Director, Mr. Naveen Pachisia, Chief Financial Officer and Mr. Arun Maheshwari, Head Finance.

items.statement: Copper price volatility may cause minor demand fluctuations but electrification growth outlook remains strong; back-to-back hedging model mitigates margin impact.
items.quote: Yes, about the demand, it may little here and there, can go a bit here and there. But as the orders position and the demand outlook is good, we do not see any, basically the demand can go slow. Because ultimately, the electrification and whatever the growth outlook we are seeing has to continue the prices sometimes go up, sometimes goes down.

items.statement: Backward integrated model produces 35-40% of copper rod requirements in-house from cathodes; 8,500+ SKUs ranging 0.07mm to 25mm; two facilities in Anand, Gujarat.
items.quote: A key pillar of our competitive advantage is our backward integrated manufacturing model. We produce oxygen -free copper rods in -house from copper cathodes meeting approximately 35 % to 40 % of our copper rod requirements internally.

items.statement: Achieved cost savings of more than INR 150 crores on an annualized basis from multiple areas including manpower reduction, travel expenses, packaging, raw material negotiations and plant operations
items.quote: During the year, we have achieved cost savings of more than INR 150 crores on an annualized basis. These efficiencies came from multiple areas, including reduction of manpower, cutting down travel expenses, reduction in reengineering of cartons and reduction of cost of packaging material, better raw material negotiations and overall plant operations of the company.

items.statement: Breakdown of INR 150 crore annualized savings: INR 80-90 crores from raw materials and plant negotiations, INR 20-25 crores from manpower reduction, INR 15 crores from travel expenses
items.quote: Where about INR80 to INR90 crores would be on raw materials. In the plant, you know, plant negotiations, we re -engineered the cartons, better negotiation with the raw material suppliers. So, INR80 to INR90 crores would be in tunes of that. INR20 to INR25 crores was in manpower, where we reduced the manpower after the unification. About INR15 crores was on travel.
